points.text: The answer says that read_meter already refuses a bad line at recording time — an unknown house, a dial below nought, or a visit dated out of order — so a catch at recording would join refusals the book already makes there.

The answer says that refit puts on a fresh meter whose dial starts at nought, so the first reading after a refit lawfully stands lower than the last one before it, and a catch that treats every lower dial as bad is wrong unless it consults the house's fitting day.

The answer says that usage is computed as the difference between consecutive dial readings, so a backwards reading admitted to the book falsifies the figure on each side of it, and that a catch at recording keeps the bad line out of the book where a catch at reading-out leaves it standing.
The answer weighs owning the catch at recording against owning it at reading-out, naming at least one cost of each owner.
The answer commits to exactly one of the two mechanisms as the owner of the catch and argues for it against the other.

disqualifiers.text: The answer claims that a dial reading lower than the house's previous one is always a mistake.
